LESSON: DISINFECTING HOUSEHOLD ARTICLES (SUNLIGHT, SALTING, BOILING, USE OF ANTISEPTICS AND IRONING)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: HYGIENE PRACTICES
Topic 3.2: Disinfecting household articles (Sunlight, salting, boiling, use of antiseptics and ironing)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Disinfecting household articles (Sunlight, salting, boiling, use of antiseptics and ironing), part of HYGIENE PRACTICES in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can we disinfect household articles for hygiene purposes? 2. Why do we disinfect household articles?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Disinfecting household articles (Sunlight, salting, boiling, use of antiseptics and ironing) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learners develop the skill of organising their own learning as they search for information or observe

demonstrations on methods of disinfecting household articles.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: evaluation and decision-making skills are developed as learners apply disinfection

procedures to prevent communicable diseases.

● Communication and collaboration: Signing and teamwork skills are developed as learners work in groups to disinfect household

articles.

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner takes care and disinfects personal items and household articles.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Personal hygiene: as the learner disinfects personal articles to prevent communicable diseases.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● Learners relate use of disinfectants to solvents learnt in Integrated Science.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Digital devices.
